17 A trolley of mass 600 kg is initially at point P on a slope, at a height of 80 m above ground level,
as shown. The trolley is released from rest and moves along the slope, first coming to rest at
point Q, at height h above ground level.
trolley
mass 600 kg
P

SCALE

80 m

slope

ground level
The total distance PQ moved by the trolley along the slope is 1.5 km. A constant resistive force of
300 N opposes the motion of the trolley on the slope.
What is h ?
A
3.5 m
B
76 m
C
79 m
D
80 m

hints: Notice the trolley is at rest at both P at 80 m and Q at height h, so kinetic energy is zero at start and finish.
Connect the loss of gravitational potential energy $mg(80-h)$ to the work done against the constant 300 N resistive force over 1.5 km.
Calculate $F \times d = 300 \times 1500$ in $\text{J}$ and equate it to $600 \times 9.81 \times (80-h)$ to solve for h.
walkthrough: Identify the energy change: initial $E_p = mg \times 80$ and final $E_p = mg \times h$ with $m = 600 \text{ kg}$. Since it starts and ends at rest, the loss is $mg(80-h)$.
State the work done against resistance: $W = Fd$ with $F = 300 \text{ N}$ and $d = 1.5 \text{ km} = 1500 \text{ m}$.
Apply conservation with work done: $mg(80-h) = W$, so $600 \times 9.81 \times (80-h) = 450000$.
Solve for the drop: $80-h = 450000 / 5886 \approx 76.5 \text{ m}$, so $h = 80 - 76.5 \approx 3.5 \text{ m}$.

A.explanation: Loss of gravitational potential energy equals work done against the 300 N force, giving $h$ about 3.5 m.

B.explanation: 76 m is the drop in height $(80-h)$, not the final height $h$ above ground level.

C.explanation: 79 m would need only a very small energy loss and ignores the $300 \text{ N} \times 1500 \text{ m}$ work done.

D.explanation: 80 m would mean no energy loss, which is impossible with a resistive force acting over 1.5 km.
